\section*{Question 6}

The derivative of a function \(f\) is defined by
\[
f^{\prime}(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{llr}
g(x) & \text { for } & -4 \leq x \leq 0 \\
5 e^{-x / 3}-3 & \text { for } & 0<x \leq 4
\end{array} .\right.
\]
The graph of the continuous function \(f^{\prime}\), shown in the figure above, has \(x\)-intercepts at \(x=-2\) and \(x=3 \ln \left(\frac{5}{3}\right)\). The graph of \(g\) on \(-4 \leq x \leq 0\)
![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/3bd01951-01dd-40be-a096-a94caa1cd628-1.jpg?height=309&width=541&top_left_y=389&top_left_x=1354) is a semicircle, and \(f(0)=5\).
(a) For \(-4<x<4\), find all values of \(x\) at which the graph of \(f\) has a point of inflection. Justify your answer.
(b) Find \(f(-4)\) and \(f(4)\).
(c) For \(-4 \leq x \leq 4\), find the value of \(x\) at which \(f\) has an absolute maximum. Justify your answer.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] \(f^{\prime}\) changes from decreasing to increasing at \(x=-2\) and from increasing to decreasing at \(x=0\). Therefore, the graph of \(f\) has points of inflection at \(x=-2\) and \(x=0\).
\item[(b)]
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(-4) & =5+\int_{0}^{-4} g(x) d x \\
& =5-(8-2 \pi)=2 \pi-3
\end{aligned}
\]
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(4) & =5+\int_{0}^{4}\left(5 e^{-x / 3}-3\right) d x \\
& =5+\left.\left(-15 e^{-x / 3}-3 x\right)\right|_{x=0} ^{x=4} \\
& =8-15 e^{-4 / 3}
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(c)] Since \(f^{\prime}(x)>0\) on the intervals \(-4<x<-2\) and
\[
\begin{aligned}
& -2<x<3 \ln \left(\frac{5}{3}\right), f \text { is increasing on the interval } \\
& -4 \leq x \leq 3 \ln \left(\frac{5}{3}\right) .
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(f^{\prime}(x)<0\) on the interval \(3 \ln \left(\frac{5}{3}\right)<x<4, f\) is
decreasing on the interval \(3 \ln \left(\frac{5}{3}\right) \leq x \leq 4\).
Therefore, \(f\) has an absolute maximum at \(x=3 \ln \left(\frac{5}{3}\right)\).
\end{itemize}
\(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { identifies } x=-2 \text { or } x=0 \\ 1: \text { answer with justification }\end{array}\right.\)
